title: corners out of reach
alt_text: Annotated equation: f n equals V n of r divided by 2r to the power n. Blue: the share of food the goat reaches. Brown: the ball’s volume, the reachable grass. Salmon: the field’s volume. Inset: stacked bars for dimensions 1 to 8, blue for the reachable share and salmon for the corners; the blue part shrinks as n grows.
takeaway: The food share is a ratio of two volumes, and the field’s corners grow faster than the ball.

title: rope length cancels
alt_text: Annotated equations in two lines: f n equals C n r to the n over 2 to the n r to the n, which equals C n over 2 to the n. Brown labels mark a ball of radius r and a field of side 2r. Blue: the unit-ball volume C n. Salmon: the unit-field volume 2 to the n. Inset: the share stays flat as the rope length changes, for n = 2, 3, and 5.
takeaway: The rope length cancels, so only the dimension decides the goat’s share.

title: never above π/8
alt_text: Annotated recurrence: f n+2 equals pi over 2 times n + 2, times f n. Blue: the share two dimensions on, and the current share. Salmon: the multiplier, at most pi/8 when n is at least 2. Inset: the multiplier for n = 2 to 12 as bars, all at or below a dashed line at pi/8.
takeaway: Because π/8 is less than ½, adding two dimensions at least halves the share once n ≥ 2.

alt_text: Annotated limit: the limit as n goes to infinity of f n equals 0. Brown: as the dimension grows without end. Blue: the share the goat can reach. Salmon: zero, which no single dimension reaches, because every share is positive.
takeaway: The share gets as small as you like, even though every finite-dimensional goat still eats something.

title: tail: 56 of 1,024
alt_text: Annotated calculation: p equals 45 + 10 + 1, divided by 2 to the 10, about 0.0547. Blue: the one-sided p-value. Black: the numbers of sequences with 8, 9, or 10 heads. Brown: 2 to the 10, the 1,024 equally likely sequences. Salmon: the result, just above alpha = 0.05. Inset: the probabilities of 0 to 10 heads in 10 fair flips, with the 8-, 9-, and 10-head tail in salmon: 56 of 1,024 sequences.
takeaway: The tail holds 56 of 1,024 sequences, so eight heads is not quite surprising enough at α = 0.05.

title: 20 tests: 64% vs 4.9%
alt_text: Annotated equations: FWER equals 1 minus 1 − alpha to the power m, and the per-test threshold alpha becomes alpha over m under Bonferroni. Salmon: the family-wise error rate, the chance of any false positive. Blue: 1 − alpha to the m, the chance that all m independent tests stay quiet, and the Bonferroni cutoff alpha over m. Brown: the per-test threshold alpha. Inset: the chance of any false positive for 1 to 60 tests; uncorrected tests at alpha = 0.05 climb to 64% at 20 tests, while Bonferroni stays just under 5%.
takeaway: Twenty independent tests at α = 0.05 give a 64% chance of at least one false positive; Bonferroni brings it back to 4.9%.
